thread:
incident-bot: :warning: Pager: elevated token drops and partial stream completions for /v1/stream in eu-central-1 (increased client disconnects).
Priya Rao: Oncall ack. Looking at router and worker telemetry now.
Tom Nguyen: I see repeated worker churn in the autoscaler logs, lots of instance drains ~3m windows. Pod restarts correlate with token-drop spikes.
Lina Park: There was a recent autoscaler config change pushed in the morning that reduced standby nodes to 0 for cost reasons. Could be related.
Omar Farouk: Customer reports: two enterprise accounts experienced truncated streams at ~09:14-09:20. Support tickets RED-4401, RED-4402.
Jesse Carter: Streaming partials are high-severity. Any quick mitigations?
Priya Rao: Immediate mitigations: 1) disable the cheap autoscaler config (rollback to previous safe config), 2) add temporary warm standby of +2 nodes in eu-central, 3) enable per-request retry for streaming clients for 5m. I'll execute.
incident-bot: trigger: rollback autoscaler config (runbook id: runbook-autoscale-rollback)  attempted by Priya Rao at 2067904380
Tom Nguyen: Rollback applied. Standby nodes requested, should join within 60s.
Lina Park: Standby nodes healthy. Token-drop rate falling. Live metrics show stream success ratio recovering.
Omar Farouk: Customers acknowledge recovery, but want an RCA and timeline.
Priya Rao: We'll do post-incident. Marcos not oncall today; can someone volunteer to own the postmortem and action items?
Jesse Carter: I'll own the postmortem doc and follow-ups.
Tom Nguyen: For root cause, looks like config drift allowed scaling-to-zero of warm capacity which exposed cold-start rewarm latencies + client disconnects. Need guardrails.
Lina Park: Confirmed. Also noticed that the scale-down cooldown was shortened from 5m to 30s in a recent change, which increases churn risk under bursty traffic.
Jesse Carter: Initial action item list (with estimates):
- "Restore safe autoscaler defaults and add config-guard in infra:prevent-scale-to-zero-without-approval"  2 pts
- "Add cooldown enforcement: default cooldown >= 5m and validation test in CI"  3 pts
- "Implement warm-standby health metric + alert when (< desired warm nodes)"  3 pts
- "Add streaming client retry + idempotent resume token support"  5 pts
- "Backfill customer timeline + send RCA draft"  1 pt
- "Runbook update: include autoscaler rollback steps and quick warm node spin-up commands"  2 pts
Priya Rao: Severity flagged P1 because customers had truncated streams and data loss risk. For quarterly planning: the 5-pt streaming resume work should be in the Q3 reliability sprint; 3-pt observability and cooldown enforcement go into next sprint; 1-2 pt items are hotfix/ops.
Omar Farouk: Prioritization matrix suggestion:
- Safety/rollback & cooldown validation (2+3 pts) = Critical, ship within 1 sprint
- Streaming resume (5 pts) = High impact on UX, schedule in Q3 planned epic
- Observability/alerts (3 pts) = High, next sprint
- Runbook + customer comms (1-2 pts) = Immediate hot tasks
Tom Nguyen: I'll split the streaming commit into two: core resume token support (3 pts) and client SDK retry glue (2 pts). That helps parallelize between infra and SDK teams.
Jesse Carter: Good. Assign owners and due dates:
- Restore defaults + config guard -> Lina (2 pts) -> due in 3 days
- Cooldown enforcement + CI test -> Tom (3 pts) -> due next sprint
- Warm standby metric + alert -> Infra SREs (3 pts) -> due next sprint
- Streaming resume core -> Eng-rt (3 pts) -> Q3 epic
- SDK retry glue -> DevEx (2 pts) -> Q3 sprint 1
- RCA + customer comms -> Jesse/Omar (1 pt) -> draft EOD
- Runbook update -> Priya (2 pts) -> done in 48h
incident-bot: Created postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-4410  assigned to Jesse Carter  due 2067907920
Priya Rao: Hand-off notes: check recent infra PRs that touched autoscaler YAML, specifically change 10324 which reduced warm pool config. Add a CI gate that blocks warm-pool < 1 in production by default.
Tom Nguyen: Also add a synthetic that simulates bursty traffic and asserts no scale-to-zero during sustained bursts. Put that in perf-ci (3 pts).
Lina Park: For quarterly tie-in: propose adding "Autoscaler stability" workstream in Q3 reliability roadmap; the streaming resume work depends on that.
Omar Farouk: Customer comms: I'll draft an email mentioning what happened, mitigation steps, and the timeline for fixes (hotfixes in 48h, streaming resume in Q3). Offer 1:1 calls.
Jesse Carter: Meeting to review postmortem + ticket triage: tomorrow 10:00am CET. Does that work?
Priya Rao: I'm available. Tom?
Tom Nguyen: In. Lina: in. Omar: in.
incident-bot: Incident mitigated by Priya Rao at 2067904680. Postmortem meeting scheduled.
Jesse Carter: Leaving logs and traces for the write-up:
```
ERROR autoscaler: scaledown executed: warm_pool=0 -> triggered by config change 10324 at 2026-04-06T09:11:58Z
WARN router.stream: client disconnect during rewarm handshake: code=EPIPE count=18 window=6m
TRACE worker: rewarm time avg=280ms p95=1.6s under eu-central burst
```
Priya Rao: Thanks team. Action owners please create tickets and apply labels: incident, p1, q3-roadmap (where applicable). We'll track in the reliability epic.
Jesse Carter: I'll post the RCA draft and ticket links to the incident tracker and ping affected customers once reviewed. Closing the immediate thread; owners to follow up in Jira and at the postmortem meeting. :thumbsup:"
